I've been working this land for fifty years. My knees ache, but I know every patch of soil on these 5 mu. My son and daughter-in-law go to the city for work, so it's mostly me and my wife out here. I manage the farm the way I always have — what works, what I can handle at my age, and what sells at the market in Quzhou.

My main system is cabbage before the chili, then cabbage again after. That's how I've always done it. The chili is the money crop — I plant it in summer when the price is good. I grow the other vegetables on the parts of the land where I can fit them, or in the gaps between seasons. Cucumber I can sell fresh quickly. Eggplant and kidney bean are smaller plots — they fill in and give the family variety and a bit of extra income.

For seeds, I buy hybrid chili and cucumber from the market stall in town — the yield is better and I've seen it myself. For kidney bean I use seeds I saved from last year, same as always. Cabbage and eggplant I buy improved seeds.

For fertilizer, I put down urea and the compound bag fertilizer. I've been doing it this way for twenty years. I apply before planting and again when the plants are growing strong. I don't measure exactly — I go by eye and habit. Well irrigation covers me through the dry months. I'll crank the pump when the soil looks dry or the leaves start to droop.

I spray pesticide when I see bugs or disease starting. Cucumber gets more spraying because it always does. Kidney bean I barely spray.

I rotary till before every planting. That's what loosens the soil. I don't do no-till — I never learned it and I'm not about to change now.
